solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dark piece of ribbon round wide-brimmed hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: only a small piece of the word ribbon is wanted, its opening letter

parts.note: O is round in shape, the usual crossword stand-in for a ring

explanation.surface: A dark band of ribbon trims the crown of a broad-brimmed hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' takes just R from ribbon, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican sombrero is the classic hat with a very broad brim.

indicators.note: sorted means put in order, so the letters of tie's are rearranged

parts.note: checkmate, or mate, is the end of a game of chess

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a tied match is settled now that the game has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' rearranges the letters of TIE'S, counting the S, to give ESTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough guess or approximate judgement.

clue.text: Peers go out together in a London suburb

parts.note: earls are members of the peerage
to court is to date or woo someone

explanation.surface: Aristocrats go on dates in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLS COURT is a district of west London, once home to a big exhibition centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court is a named district in the west of the capital.

indicators.note: cracked suggests broken apart, so the letters of in game are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle is solved during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' looks like solving the riddle; it rearranges IN GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery, a synonym for riddle.

indicators.note: after puts the theologian behind the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar goes out fishing after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is a standard crossword 'game', and DD a standard 'theologian'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Prison term given by one lacking awareness? Just the opposite

indicators.note: lacking signals that something goes missing from a word
this reverses the stated roles: it is awareness that lacks one, not one lacking awareness

parts.note: sentience is the capacity to feel and be aware
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A jail term is handed down by someone oblivious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'one lacking awareness' would remove SENTIENCE from I; 'Just the opposite' says take I out of SENTIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the punishment, often a period in jail, a court passes.

parts.note: one means a single individual
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a feeling is unrequited.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way feeling or arrangement is not returned by the other party.

clue.text: Oppose all others crossing small island

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so all others spans the island

parts.note: the rest are all the others
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Everyone else objects to crossing a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all others' could suggest a word for everyone; here it is the leftover lot, the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or fight against something.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A family member works at the US base at Quantico in intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across quantiCO US INtelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle.

indicators.note: flighty means fickle and unsettled, so the letters of Sudanese are rearranged

explanation.surface: A capricious dancer from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseuse is the French word for a female dancer, used for a ballerina.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the notice wraps round the card game

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone has read and absorbed a notice about a bridge game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digested' looks like a past-tense verb about eating; it means condensed, as in a digest.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a shortened version, so a digested text is condensed.

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a lapse is a failing or slip

explanation.surface: A student is ultimately failing to pass the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of Undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass by.

indicators.note: not initially says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: preparation, the act of making plans, is here taken as plans

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether plans are revised, but not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' removes P from the front of PREPARATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends means offering compensation for a wrong.

clue.text: Utterly unwise to discard spades, senseless

indicators.note: to discard means to throw out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: insane is used for something utterly unwise or foolish
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Throwing away spades at cards would be idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discard' removes S from INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, lacking sense.

parts.note: over means left over, remaining
a bank statement is a financial record

explanation.surface: An outstanding bank statement reveals reckless spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Overstatement is exaggeration, extravagance of expression.

clue.text: City in Brazil surrounded by delightful lake

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the city goes within the delightful word

parts.note: super means delightful, excellent
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

explanation.surface: A Brazilian city lies next to a beautiful lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Brazilian lake, but the lake is in North America, on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior is the largest of the North American Great Lakes.

clue.text: Service uniform, good worn by lad

indicators.note: worn by sets the good letter onto the end of the lad

parts.note: even means uniform or regular
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A church service at which a boy wears a smart uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' puts G after SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening church service in the Anglican tradition.

clue.text: Reportedly call boy to find a spice

indicators.note: reportedly signals something spoken, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: to term is to call or name, and Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently summoning a lad to find a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM ERIC, said aloud, matches the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow spice from a ginger-family root, used in curries.

parts.note: a hovel is a shabby shed or hut

explanation.surface: A miner keeps a tool in a little shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a spade-like tool for digging and moving coal.

clue.text: Pay, unfortunately, has risen on railway

indicators.note: risen, in a down clue, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: alas is an expression meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Sadly, fares have gone up on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risen' turns ALAS to SALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is the fixed pay an employee receives.

clue.text: Spotted blunder by Greek character in retirement flat occasionally used?

parts.note: pied means spotted or blotchy

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawal, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to err is to blunder
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone spots an error by a Greek on his retirement flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses ERRETA to ATERRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second home kept for occasional stays.

indicators.note: in the middle of tells us the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A fan, as the word appears in a conventional dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across roAD DICTionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict, informally, is a keen fan or enthusiast.

clue.text: A few words from Lear finally entering stage

indicators.note: entering puts that letter inside the stage

parts.note: a phase is a stage

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lines from King Lear spoken on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, the last letter of Lear, which goes inside PHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a small group of words.

parts.note: a side is a team
a step is a pace

explanation.surface: Someone eludes a team using speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to dodge or evade something.

clue.text: Catch horse after start of steeplechase

indicators.note: after places the horse behind that letter
start of takes the first letter

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse is snagged after the start of a steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives S, and NAG follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a catch or hidden drawback.

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: free means loose, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A route into free flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges INTO to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is flying aircraft, the business of flight.

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is removed

parts.note: Candida is a play by George Bernard Shaw

explanation.surface: An outspoken Shaw drama is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last A of CANDIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and open in speech.

clue.text: Dramatist is wary, possibly put in dangerous situation

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a plight is a dangerous or difficult situation

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement, so the letters of wary are mixed

explanation.surface: A dramatist is cautious when placed in peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is just a link; the surface's dangerous situation becomes the outer word, holding AYWR, the letters of WARY mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright is a writer of plays, a dramatist.
